title: E-motion Capture: AI missed our intentions by focusing on our words.
subtitle: What my Tweets, in the dying days of Twitter, say about me...
text:
The following is generated off of TwitterGPT, which I strongly suspect will require a threads instance. It's a meditation, inadvertently, on the difference between artificial intelligence based in the language we use versus the things we mean. reporting!

Subscribe now

Based on a close examination of the recent tweets of (ok, on X/Twitter it’s scottmuirMD),

“several insights1 can be gathered about their2 professional interests, affiliations, and potential areas of expertise.

It is important to note3 that the user's recent tweets contain a mix of retweets, replies, and original tweets, making it challenging to determine their primary focus4. However, here are six distinct observations5

• he engages with various medical professionals and experts, such as Dr. Winarick, Dr. Plantel, and , suggesting a connection to the medical field.

This is what is suggests.6

I’m also kind of into this degree of pseudo-tentative presentation of data.

• The user retweets posts related to mental health, including discussions on personality disorders, obsessive-compulsive personality, and narcissism. This indicates a potential interest or involvement in psychology or psychiatry.

There is a potential interest, I agree.

• He shares a post about weight loss, suggesting a possible interest in health and wellness beyond mental health.

Again, remarkably… tentative! Given artificial intelligence seems to have an enthusiasm for overly broad statements and made up assertions, this level of tentative is amusing7.

• The user retweets a post about a new medical device, a full-body scan machine combined with a proprietary EMR (electronic medical records) system. This implies an interest in technological advancements in the medical field.

Even ChatGPT trained on Twitter can tell I'm into fMRI guided treatment like SAINT…but also can't tell what it is. It is not a full body scan machine and it's not combined with a Proprietary EHR, but that's a great med tech company, thanks ChatGPT! In the meanwhile, it is probably worth noting I am a practicing psychiatrist in New York…and if you want your psychiatric treatment of the future, call me, maybe?8

• He retweets a post about the world being hostile to girls, indicating a concern for gender-related issues and potentially advocating for gender equality.

“Potentially advocating” for gender equality is about as good as anyone's gonna get on Twitter these days.

• The user engages with various individuals and retweets posts from different sources, suggesting an open-mindedness and willingness to explore diverse perspectives.

No wonder nothing I say goes viral. Willingness to explore diverse perspectives? That is just death on the Internet. I am destined for extremely niche status as a person who says reasonable things to other reasonable people at best. Nobody's ever gonna pay attention to that.

• Based on the tweets, it is challenging to determine Political allegiances or home city. However, their professional interests seem to revolve around the medical field, with a particular focus on mental health, psychology, and technological advancements.

Here, at least, it sticks the landing. I have a particular focus on mental health, as a Psychiatrist I'm more engaged with psychological ideas than most, and I do have a focus on technological advancements. It is not wrong.

• Personality-wise, it is difficult to ascertain OCEAN personality profile with certainty. However, their tweets indicate a sense of humor, as they retweet posts with repetitive quacks and engage in lighthearted banter with other users.

When I die, my tombstone will ready:

“a sense of humor as indicated by engagement lighthearted banter and a series of repetitive quacks.”

It also comes up with a gift recommendation, which is good enough, while at the same time missing the mark in a number of important respects:

• Consider getting them the book "The Body Keeps the Score: Brain, Mind, and Body in the Healing of Trauma" by Bessel van der Kolk.

Gift giving is hard.

I still think using artificial intelligence is under performing because people aren't using it to snow hospital systems with complaints for the lack of 501r Compliance….more seriously, however:

We have been underwhelmed, and we should've expected that. The problem with AI is that it was trained on humans. Humans dissatisfy each other all day long. The Internet is a horrible place to learn how to be helpful to humans. The training data is humans being useless to each other. The average of those answers, which is the lifeblood of ChatGPT, is almost by definition going to be milquetoast and unsatisfying.

We are not there yet. Not by a long shot. At least when it comes to trying to figure out what I am into on Twitter. It can say things that are as unsurprising and tentative as you could hope.

Being a human is hard. Training a human simulacra on humans and what they cranked out between liking cat videos is harder. Then feeding them their own output inadvertently becomes expensive gruel leading to an “obesity of language.” It becomes relentlessly more boring, more pedantic, and less satisfying with each piece of underwhelming “training data” fed into it. Ignoring idiots might be more important than the volume of language that those idiots cranked out. Or maybe we're not so dumb?

We are yearn for the extraordinary, but drive straight into the brick wall of everything one person said to another for the history of the Internet.

Humans are predictable, polite, profane, but perhaps most importantly, don't always say what we are really thinking. There is a lot of implicit understanding going on even in the most explicit of writing. The inability to factor that in—we are polite liars—in the service of not offending each other, or purposely offending each other, is what makes us remarkable. We didn't need ChatGPT to train and what we said, we needed it to train and what we actually meant. And that's …a different task.

Who could've predicted?

1I don't think these things count as insights. Insights are things that are not obvious. I’be seen a lot of companies that offer to sell insights, and unfortunately, I'm not sure the understand what insightful is. Insights are things that are not obvious but that a human can tell, or any refined enough intelligence, by understanding something other than what is on the surface.

2They/them pronouns is just easier as a default pronoun. I am both a fan of gender affirming pronouns, but also easy answers to otherwise complex questions.

3This is not really important to note.

4This is absolutely on purpose.

5Observations are not insights. They are in fact the opposite of insights. They’re outsights, at best.

6It under-rates my degree of sh$tposting betwixt myself and my medical tech friends. “Engaged—but with a degree of grim irony.”

7What happened to “go big or go home”?

8I will also never get tired of Carly Rae Jepsen jokes.
